# Godhajātaka (Ja 138)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Godhajātaka* (Ja 138) is a canonical birth-story preserved in the *Jātaka* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Set in the Jetavana monastery, the frame story relates that the Buddha addressed a deceitful monk (*kuhaka*) and delivered a tale of the past to expose his hypocritical nature [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. In the past, during the reign of King Brahmadatta of Bārāṇasī, the Bodhisatta was reborn as a lizard (*godha*) living in an anthill near a forest hermitage [Fausböll 1877]. When an unscrupulous, deceitful ascetic (*kūṭatāpasa*) attempted to snare and kill the lizard to eat its meat, the Bodhisatta eluded him by taking refuge inside his mound and delivered the moralizing stanza opening with *Kiṁ te jaṭāhi dummedha* ("What is the use of your matted hair, you fool?") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. Concluding the narrative (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the false ascetic with the hypocritical monk, an earlier virtuous ascetic with Sāriputta, and the lizard with himself [Fausböll 1877].

The central verse of the *Godhajātaka* is an ancient Buddhist stanza preserved as verse 394 of the Pali *Dhammapada* in the *Brāhmaṇavagga* [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral identifies wide cross-tradition parallels to this verse across the early Buddhist textual corpus, including the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp, *Brammaṇavagga*; G3-Dhp 61–70), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 33, *Brahmanavarga*), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 33), and several early Chinese translations, namely T 210, T 212, and T 213 [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes a parallel relationship with another Pali lizard tale, the *Godharājajātaka* (Ja 325) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records no Pali-internal or cross-language matches exceeding its minimum match threshold (score ≥ 10) [DharmaNexus].
